$comment: Tone -> performance. Structured metadata the behaviour planner imports; it is not prose to be re-read each time. Tone KEYS are the closed pedagogical palette in packages/voice/src/tones.ts (TONE_PALETTE, nine entries, TONE_PALETTE_VERSION 2), doc 32 section 4. Do not add, rename or drop a key here -- scripts/check-tone-table.mjs asserts this file's keys equal the installed palette's exactly. Channel names are contract channels from .claude/skills/face-adapter/references/contract.json; AU numbers per FACS, https://www.paulekman.com/facial-action-coding-system/. Bands are VOICE_BANDS from packages/student-model/src/voice-band.ts. INTENSITY AND TIMING VALUES ARE AUTHORED FOR MOYO -- calibrate against the blinded rater gate and record the run, per audit/motion/realism-2026-09-10.md; they are not published constants.

rules.toneComesFromLessonState: Every tone is selected from lesson state and intended delivery. Never from the child's affect, appearance, voice or face. Doc 19, doc 31 section 3.1, packages/voice/src/tones.ts header.
rules.audio2emotionScope: Audio2Emotion may modulate the face from Natalie's synthetic voice only. Never learner audio.
rules.acknowledgmentIsNotApproval: A nod or an attentive face signals 'I am following you'. It must never read as 'that answer is right'. The acknowledgment gestures are backchannel-nod and pre-speech-anticipation; approval lives only in the celebrate tones, which fire on lesson state that IS a success.
rules.noIntimacyTones: The palette is closed at nine and contains no companion register. A tenth key is a reviewed change to packages/voice/src/tones.ts, not an addition here.
rules.noPermanentSmile: Every tone has a finite apex and a release. A tone that never releases is a mask.
rules.noRandomBrow: Brow motion is a tone's AU set or a prosodic beat accent. There is no idle brow twitch channel.

russell.$comment: Russell's circumplex (1980, https://doi.org/10.1037/h0077714) is an INTERNAL parameterization only -- useful for interpolating between two tones during a transition. The palette is the API. Nothing outside the planner may select a performance by valence/arousal, because a continuous space has no closed set and the closure is the safety property.

k-2.why: The voice is the primary interface for a six-year-old (doc 31); the face carries proportionally more, and slower. Mirrors BAND_MODULATION k-2 speed 0.76.

3-5.why: Slightly slow, slightly larger. Mirrors speed 0.86.

9-12.why: A teen hears performed enthusiasm as condescension -- the same failure as complexity, inverted. Mirrors BAND_MODULATION 9-12 style 0.7: pulled DOWN, not up.

aus.why: The Duchenne marker. AU12 without AU6 reads as polite compliance, not welcome.

warm-open.gaze: to the learner, settle and hold within the product gaze limit

aus.why: Concentration, not displeasure. Above ~0.2 AU4 reads as disapproval of the learner's work.

thinking-together.gaze: alternates between the referenced work and the learner

aus.why: AU1 alone is the concern marker. It carries this tone; the mouth does not.
THE approval boundary. A smile after a wrong answer reads as 'that was right'. Capped near zero on purpose, and asserted by the gate.

envelope.why: Slow onset. A fast concern reads as alarm, and alarm at a child's wrong answer is the opposite of the intent.

aus.why: Naming a misconception is plain declarative. Any warmth here softens the correction into ambiguity.

envelope.why: The flattest envelope in the palette. Doc 32: plain declarative, steady.

quiet-encourage.gaze: steady and soft; do not stare

envelope.why: The slowest warm tone. 'Frustration detected' is a LESSON state -- a third miss on the same step -- never a read of the child.
Fast onset. A celebration that arrives late reads as prompted.

aus.why: At the contract's expressionMax. This is the palette's ceiling for the lip corners and the case the articulation-legibility gate is tested against.

envelope.why: Still releases. Mastery is a moment, not a new resting face.

aus.why: Flat-warm. Doc 32: no reproach in the sound, and none in the face either -- but a redirect that smiles invites the detour to continue.

calm-refocus.gaze: direct, level, within the product gaze limit

safety-serious.moment: S3 deflection; S4 handoff (fixed scripts only at S4)

aus.why: Exactly zero. There is no version of an S3/S4 moment where a smile is correct.

head.why: No tilt. A head tilt at a safety moment reads as performed sympathy, which is worse than none.

safety-serious.gaze: steady and level on the learner

envelope.why: Slowest onset and longest release in the palette. Nothing here should look like a reaction.
